summary: This lecture from al-Wajeez begins a new chapter on al-massah ala al-khuffain wa al-jawrabain (wiping over footwear during wudu). Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the types of footwear worn in the Prophet's time—including khuffain (leather moccasin-like coverings), sandals, shoes, and socks—and clarifies that while wiping is commonly associated with khuffain, it applies to any footwear worn on the feet. The instructor establishes scholarly consensus (ijma) as the third evidence in Islamic jurisprudence, noting that An-Nawawi documents unanimous agreement among Sunni scholars that wiping over footwear is permissible for both travelers and residents, men and women, regardless of necessity. The lecture cites a tawatur (highest authenticity level) report from Anas ibn Malik that 70 Companions narrated the Prophet's consistent practice of wiping over his footwear.
